what_its_for: This medicine replaces or adds to the thyroid hormone that your body is not making enough of. It is used to treat an underactive thyroid gland (hypothyroidism). It helps your body work normally by restoring thyroid hormone levels.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, usually once a day in the morning on an EMPTY stomach, at least 30 to 60 minutes before you eat breakfast. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so your body gets a steady level of the medicine. Do NOT stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel fine.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over weeks based on blood tests and how you feel. The right dose is different for every person. Never change your dose on your own. Common starting doses are low (for example, 30 mg once daily) and are adjusted until your thyroid levels are in the normal range. Always follow exactly what your doctor tells you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose as scheduled. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss several doses in a row, call your doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, or vitamins with iron within 4 hours of taking your thyroid medicine — these can block your body from absorbing it. Avoid eating foods high in fiber (like bran) right before or after your dose. Avoid switching between different brands of thyroid medicine without your doctor's approval, as each brand may work slightly differently. Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice close to the time you take your medicine. Do not take more than prescribed — too much can cause a fast or irregular heartbeat.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: chest pain or a very fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat; severe headache; shortness of breath; feeling extremely shaky or anxious; heavy sweating; high fever; sudden weight loss; or swelling of your ankles or feet. Also call your doctor if you are still feeling tired, gaining weight, feeling cold all the time, or have other signs that the medicine may not be working.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within the first 1 to 2 weeks, but it often takes 6 to 8 weeks or longer before you feel the full benefit. Your doctor will check blood tests (TSH, T3, T4) regularly to make sure the dose is right for you. Most people need to take thyroid medicine for the rest of their life.
special_populations: OLDER ADULTS: Your doctor may start you on an even lower dose and increase it more slowly to avoid putting stress on your heart. PREGNANCY: It is very important to keep taking your thyroid medicine during pregnancy. Your dose may need to be increased. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. CHILDREN: This medicine is used in children, but the dose must be carefully chosen by your doctor based on your child's age and weight. HEART CONDITIONS: If you have heart disease, your doctor will be extra careful about your dose because too much thyroid hormone can strain the heart. Always tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
